# DefinitionWriteOptions

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Options for writing a document as a definition.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core/definition`.

## Properties

- [`embedResources`](#embedresources): Always carry resource bytes in the definition (`data`), even where `resourceRef` would name them.
- [`onUnrepresentable`](#onunrepresentable): What to do with a construct a definition cannot express.
- [`resourceRef`](#resourceref): Names a resource the host can supply again when the definition is read.
- [`target`](#target): The definition version to write, `"1.0"`.
- [`writePaletteTokens`](#writepalettetokens): Write a palette token (`slate-800`) where a colour equals a palette entry exactly, instead of hex.

### `embedResources`

```typescript
embedResources?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

Always carry resource bytes in the definition (`data`), even where `resourceRef` would name them.

### `onUnrepresentable`

```typescript
onUnrepresentable?: "drop" | "error" | undefined
```

*optional*

What to do with a construct a definition cannot express. `'error'` (the default) throws a [`DefinitionError`](definition-error.md) listing all of them and writes nothing; `'drop'` leaves each out and reports a `dropped` note, after which the result is not a faithful copy.

### `resourceRef`

```typescript
resourceRef?: ((resource: DefinitionResourceDescriptor) => string | undefined | Promise<string | undefined>) | undefined
```

*optional*

Names a resource the host can supply again when the definition is read. Return a name and the definition carries `ref` and a `sha256` instead of the bytes; return `undefined` to embed them. The writer never invents a name.

### `target`

```typescript
target?: string | undefined
```

*optional*

The definition version to write, `"1.0"`. Anything this release cannot write is refused.

### `writePaletteTokens`

```typescript
writePaletteTokens?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

Write a palette token (`slate-800`) where a colour equals a palette entry exactly, instead of hex.
